candidates.title: Jung's UFO book: from mass rumor to 'and yet they're on radar'
candidates.quote: And then as the book goes on, it's like it's getting harder for him to dismiss it though. And if you've read it like at the end he's like and yet they're on radar.
documents: Flying Saucers: A Modern Myth of Things Seen in the Skies

link.reason: Both are about Carl Jung's book Flying Saucers. This telling describes how the book's argument shifts as it goes on.
link.difference: Adds that Jung starts by treating saucers as mass rumor, finds them harder to dismiss as the book goes on, and ends by noting they show up on radar.
